items.defectStatement: The mutual-exclusion validators test truthiness instead of field presence, allowing a report with both age=0 and timestamp=0 to validate. If only one value is zero and the other is nonzero, the other validator still rejects the report.
obligations: Reject reports containing both age and timestamp, including when both equal zero.
Continue accepting otherwise valid reports containing only either field, including zero.
Preserve existing field constraints and do not introduce a requirement that either field be present.
items.notes: The finding overstates the bypass: one zero alone does not bypass both validators; both numeric values must be zero.

items.defectStatement: The validation-failure warning includes the entire unvalidated browser report in raw_report, exposing caller-controlled and potentially sensitive report contents in application logs.
obligations: Remove raw report contents from the validation-failure log.
Avoid logging arbitrary input values through replacement metadata or validation-error messages.
Preserve validation rejection and the existing HTTP 422 response.
items.notes: Deleting this warning or retaining only safe metadata is also valid. Serializer errors can echo invalid inputs. Other raw-payload logs elsewhere remain separate issues.

items.defectStatement: The endpoint queries Snuba before checking enable_error_context, so opt-out requests incur an unnecessary replay lookup and can fail when Snuba is unavailable.
obligations: Skip query_replay_instance and error-detail fetching when enable_error_context is false.
Preserve case-insensitive flag handling and the default enabled behavior.
Continue paginating recording segments and analyzing them with an empty error-event list for opt-out requests.
Preserve the existing replay lookup and error enrichment for enabled requests.
items.exampleFix:
if request.query_params.get("enable_error_context", "true").lower() == "false":
            return self.paginate(
                request=request,
                paginator_cls=GenericOffsetPaginator,
                data_fn=functools.partial(fetch_segments_metadata, project.id, replay_id),
                on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, []),
            )

        filter_params = self.get_filter_params(request, project)

        # Fetch the replay's error IDs from the replay_id.
        snuba_response = query_replay_instance(
            project_id=project.id,
            replay_id=replay_id,
            start=filter_params["start"],
            end=filter_params["end"],
            organization=project.organization,
            request_user_id=request.user.id,
        )
items.notes: An early return makes this locally fixable using the pagination call shown in the frozen input. Merely guarding the query without initializing snuba_response breaks subsequent processing.

items.defectStatement: Both custom cell-renderer paths use truthiness to decide whether to accept a result, replacing valid results such as 0, an empty string, null, or false with default content.
obligations: Honor every custom body-renderer result except undefined.
Honor every custom header-renderer result except undefined.
Preserve default rendering when a renderer is absent or returns undefined.
items.notes: Changing the cited body condition to cell !== undefined fixes only the body. The finding also requires changing the header condition at line 32.

items.defectStatement: Each paginated summary request passes the replay's entire error_ids list to fetch_error_details before pagination, causing nodestore to load all corresponding full event payloads without a bound.
obligations: Bound the number of error IDs passed to fetch_error_details by a fixed positive limit.
Apply the bound before fetching full event payloads.
Preserve opt-out behavior and handling of empty replay results.
Continue including error context for enabled requests.
items.notes: 100 is an illustrative cap, not a mandated value. Capping before retrieval addresses this finding; caching across pages and bounding the preceding Snuba response are separate changes.

items.defectStatement: The empty-search branch returns all sorted attributes before hidden-attribute filtering runs, exposing is_segment, project_id, and received in the default view and for whitespace-only searches.
obligations: Exclude all HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES for empty, whitespace-only, and nonempty searches.
Preserve the existing attribute ordering.
Preserve trimmed, case-insensitive name matching for visible attributes.
items.notes: The defective early return is at lines 61–62, outside the anchor. Replacing only the later filter cannot affect that already-returned result.

items.defectStatement: The completion test supplies max_segment_id=None but mocks delete_matched_rows, preventing execution of _make_recording_filenames. It therefore does not detect removal of the production None guard.
obligations: Add regression coverage that executes the real filename-generation helper with max_segment_id=None.
Assert that this case produces an empty filename list without raising.
Ensure removal of the None guard causes the regression test to fail.
Preserve the existing bulk-job completion assertions.
items.notes: Coverage-only finding: the production guard already exists, and replacing fixture data cannot supply the missing test. The frozen input omits the helper's implementation and import location.
